insights.claim: The Konflux Dockerfile explicitly removes the OpenSSL FIPS provider (openssl-fips-provider-so), making this container image incompatible with FIPS-validated deployments.
insights.reasoning: Line 63 of the Konflux Dockerfile runs `rpm -e --nodeps openssl-fips-provider-so || true`, which removes the FIPS cryptographic provider from the UBI 9 base image. This is a deliberate build-time decision that prevents the image from operating in FIPS mode, even on clusters with FIPS enforcement enabled. This is architecturally significant for regulated deployments.

insights.claim: vllm-gaudi uses the vLLM out-of-tree (OOT) platform plugin model, registering HpuPlatform with PlatformEnum.OOT to avoid forking the upstream vLLM codebase.
insights.reasoning: The plugin architecture allows this repository to focus exclusively on Gaudi/HPU acceleration while inheriting the full vLLM serving stack (API server, scheduling, batching) from the upstream package installed at build time. This decoupling means HTTP endpoints, authentication, and API behavior are upstream-owned and not directly configurable from this repo's source.

insights.claim: This repository contains no Kubernetes manifests, services, or deployment resources; all runtime orchestration is delegated to the RHOAI platform's KServe ServingRuntime definitions.
insights.reasoning: The analyzer confirmed null services, null deployments, and no kustomization files. The repository produces a container image only. Service exposure, routing, scaling, and authentication are entirely platform-managed. This means architecture properties like network services, ingress, and RBAC are not extractable from this repo and must be documented at the platform or KServe level.
